nodes.label: PandaPools — Android
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: Native Android constant-product AMM for Minima; MIT-licensed original code bundling Apache-2.0 Minima components (minimaapi.aar); release variant debug-signed for install parity; build pinned to JBR 21.

nodes.label: Constant-Product AMM over Aggregated Micro-Pools
nodes.rationale: Swaps are routed across every pool for a pair (water-filling by best price) and settle in one all-or-nothing transaction. LPs earn the 0.5% fee which accrues inside the pool (K grows) — deliberately no LP token.

nodes.label: 0.5% Pool Covenant (unique address per pool)
nodes.rationale: A pool is two reserve coins at a unique covenant address — the covenant's params are hardcoded literals, so the address is its script hash. Every post is gated on the covenant's own txncheck verdict; all fund math is exact (grain-floored, pool-favourable rounding).

nodes.label: KMIN Product Floor
nodes.rationale: The covenant enforces the constant-product invariant with a KMIN product floor specifically to defeat a dust-pairing drain that is unique to the UTXO/2-coin pool model.

nodes.label: 5-Layer Pool Recovery
nodes.rationale: Durable recipe persistence, re-track-on-launch, backup/restore, and faded-beacon re-announce, so the user can always find and withdraw pools even after a node resync or on a new device.

nodes.label: minimaapi Broadcast-Intent IPC
nodes.rationale: The app talks to a local Minima Core node on-device via the minimaapi broadcast-Intent IPC — no remote custodian or server.

nodes.label: PandaPools MiniDapp (shared registry sibling)
nodes.author: eurobuddha
nodes.rationale: The Android app shares the same mainnet registry and 0.5% covenant as the MiniDapp, so both trade the same live pools.
